1.mascotDialogue: It is insertion sort, simply given permission to take large steps first. Shrink the gap enough times, and it collapses into ordinary insertion sort for the final, finest pass.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 2's gap begins at n divided by 2, halving each outer pass. Lines 6 through 8 are only insertion sort's inner loop, comparing arr[j] to arr[j minus gap] instead of arr[j minus 1].

3.mascotDialogue: Watch these first comparisons leap across three positions at once — this is a gap of 3 performing long-distance correction, before the finer gap-of-1 pass even begins.

4.mascotDialogue: This is a quiet kind of mistake — the output is correct, yet the algorithm has silently stopped being the algorithm it claims to be. Not every mistake crashes. Some simply discard, quietly, the entire reason you chose this approach.
